The Northern Betsimisaraka dialect originates from the Austronesian migrations to Madagascar, which occurred around 650 CE, when proto-Malagasy speakers from the Barito River region of southeastern Borneo arrived on the island's southeast coast via maritime routes. It is also the popular dialect of the city of Toamasina (Tamatave), and is used by members of the Northern Betsimisaraka diaspora residing in the capital city, Antananarivo.
